metadata.title: feat: service-account support and pre-invoke security hardening
metadata.author: jonpspri

description:
## Summary

- Add `skip_onboarding` parameter to `EmailAuthService.create_user()` to skip personal team creation, role assignment, and registration event logging for service accounts / synthetic users
- Add `ensure_user_exists()` idempotent helper with race-condition handling for concurrent user creation
- Use `!disabled` sentinel hash for passwordless service accounts (non-loginable by design)
- Inject user identity and tool/gateway metadata into plugin `GlobalContext` during pre-invoke hooks
- Run `HTTP_PRE_REQUEST` plugin hooks before internal MCP authentication so token-exchange plugins can transform headers
- Make docker-compose env vars configurable with defaults (`PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS`, `STREAMABLE_HTTP_MAX_EVENTS_PER_STREAM`, `LOCUST_WXO_AUTH_ENABLED`, `HTTPX_*`)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `skip_onboarding` (no team, no role, no registration event)
- [x] Unit tests for `ensure_user_exists` (create, existing, race condition, re-raise, email normalization, skip_onboarding forwarding)
- [x] Unit test for failed-registration audit still fires even with `skip_onboarding`
- [x] Unit tests for pre-invoke user injection and tool/gateway metadata injection into global context
- [x] Unit test for pre-request plugin hooks running before internal MCP auth
- [x] All 775 tests pass, linters clean (ruff warnings pre-existing)

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: `ensure_user_exists()` calls `create_user()` with `password=""` while `skip_onboarding` defaults to `False`. In `create_user()`, empty passwords only bypass hashing when `skip_onboarding=True`; otherwise `hash_password_async("")` raises `ValueError`, so `ensure_user_exists()` will fail for the default case. Consider either (a) forcing `skip_onboarding=True` for this helper, (b) requiring/providing a non-empty password (e.g., generated) when `skip_onboarding=False`, or (c) adding a `password` parameter so callers choose explicitly.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The `ensure_user_exists()` docstring says `skip_onboarding` skips “audit events”, but `create_user()` still logs a failed registration event on exceptions even when `skip_onboarding=True` (and the PR test plan explicitly expects that auditing). Please adjust the wording to match the actual semantics (e.g., success-path onboarding/audit events are skipped, but failure auditing is still recorded).

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: This test intends to verify that `HTTP_PRE_REQUEST` hooks transform headers *before* auth runs, but it currently doesn’t assert that `run_pre_request_hooks()` was invoked (or that the transformed headers were actually used to build the auth scope / passed into `streamable_http_auth`). As written, it could still pass even if pre-request hooks are skipped. Consider capturing the `scope["headers"]` seen by the auth function and/or using an `AsyncMock` to assert `run_pre_request_hooks` was awaited with the original headers and that the downstream auth sees the transformed headers.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The `ensure_user_exists_creates_new_user` test stubs `create_user()`, so it won’t catch real failures from the current implementation (e.g., empty password hashing when `skip_onboarding` is left at its default). Once `ensure_user_exists()` behavior is finalized, consider adding at least one test that exercises the real `create_user()` path (or asserts the exact args passed to `create_user()`, including the `skip_onboarding`/password interaction) to prevent regressions.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Good catch. Fixed in 289c333 — changed the sentinel guard from `not password and skip_onboarding` to `not password and skip_password_validation`. The latter is the actual invariant for non-loginable accounts and correctly covers `ensure_user_exists(skip_onboarding=False)`.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Agreed — updated both docstrings in 289c333 to clarify that `skip_onboarding` skips success-path events only; failure-path audit events are always recorded.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Good point. Fixed in 289c333 — replaced the plain function with an `AsyncMock` and added an assertion that `run_pre_request_hooks` was awaited with the original headers (`mock_run_hooks.call_args.kwargs["headers"] == original_headers`).

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Acknowledged. The existing `test_ensure_user_exists_passes_skip_onboarding` already asserts exact kwargs forwarded to `create_user` (including `password=""`, `skip_password_validation=True`), which catches plumbing regressions. The underlying risk — `hash_password_async("")` failing with default `skip_onboarding=False` — is now eliminated by the sentinel guard fix in 289c333. An integration-style test would add value but is outside scope of this PR.

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Reviewed and rebased onto main. All 814 tests in affected files pass.

**Changes made during review:**

1. **Rebase conflict resolution** — 3 trivial `docker-compose.yml` conflicts (inline comments on HTTPX env vars, `LOCUST_WXO_AUTH_ENABLED` default `true` → kept `false` as safer default). After rebase, stale diffs from already-merged PRs (session_pool, .env.example, config.py, etc.) dropped off cleanly.

2. **Docstring clarification** — Narrowed the `skip_onboarding` docstring claim from "failure-path audit events are always recorded" to specify that only *unexpected*-failure events (`except Exception` path) are always recorded. Duplicate-user rejections (`UserExistsError`, `IntegrityError`) are intentionally not audited — they're normal control flow for idempotent patterns like `ensure_user_exists()`.

**Review findings — all clear:**

- **Security**: `!disabled` sentinel is safe — `verify_password()` catches `InvalidHash` and returns `False`. User injection fallback only populates `GlobalContext.user` when `None`, preventing overwrite. Race-condition handling in `ensure_user_exists` is correct (check → create → catch → re-fetch → re-raise if still missing).
- **Consistency**: `ensure_user_exists()` follows established `ensure_personal_team()` pattern. Tool/gateway metadata injection matches `invoke_tool()` path. Pre-request hooks placement mirrors Python middleware chain.
- **Test coverage**: 100% differential coverage — 13 new tests cover all new code paths (skip_onboarding, ensure_user_exists, user/metadata injection, pre-request hooks).
- **Performance**: No concerns — no new DB queries on hot paths.

commits.message:
fix: auth-header override guard bypass with mixed-case keys

The `overridden` set stored original-case plugin header keys, but the
filter compared lowercased keys against it. A plugin returning
"Authorization" (mixed-case) instead of "authorization" would bypass
the plugins_can_override_auth_headers=false guard and overwrite inbound
auth headers.

Fix: normalize `overridden` to lowercase so the filter comparison is
case-insensitive. Add a deny-path test for mixed-case auth headers.

Also document the known limitation that pre-invoke hooks may run twice
when Rust direct execution fails and falls back to the Python path.
Pre-invoke plugins must be idempotent for correctness on this path.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: plugin context parity and double pre-invoke on Rust fallback

Two issues addressed:

1. Context parity: prepare_rust_mcp_tool_execution() now accepts
   plugin_global_context and plugin_context_table from the resolve
   handler, reusing the middleware-provided GlobalContext (which carries
   JWT claims state, correlation ID, and user identity). Tool/gateway
   metadata is injected before pre-invoke hooks run, matching the
   invoke_tool() pattern. The resolve handler extracts these from
   request.state and passes them through.

2. Double pre-invoke prevention: When Rust direct execution fails and
   falls back to /_internal/mcp/tools/call, Rust now injects an
   x-contextforge-pre-invoke-ran header. invoke_tool() checks for this
   header and skips re-running TOOL_PRE_INVOKE hooks, preventing double
   execution for non-idempotent plugins (rate limiters, token exchange,
   audit hooks).

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
feat: auth service-layer refactor and pre-invoke security hardening

Extend EmailAuthService for plugin-driven user provisioning:
- add skip_onboarding parameter to create_user() so auth plugins can
  create synthetic/service users without onboarding side-effects
- add ensure_user_exists() for idempotent user creation
- skip password hashing for empty-password service accounts

Harden pre-invoke plugin hook path:
- replace header-based skip_pre_invoke derivation with an explicit
  parameter threaded through the internal RPC path, preventing external
  callers from spoofing x-contextforge-pre-invoke-ran to bypass
  TOOL_PRE_INVOKE security plugins

Include design spec and implementation plan for the broader auth plugin
service-layer refactor (eliminating direct DB access from wxo auth
plugin, replacing wxo_team_tokens SQL table with L1/L2 cache).

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>

- Clarify docstrings: skip_onboarding skips success-path events only;
  failure auditing is always recorded
- Strengthen pre-request hook test to assert run_pre_request_hooks
  was awaited with the original headers
